cards.back: An idea you can test, often written as a prediction with a reason.
cards.say: hypothesis. An idea you can test, often written as a prediction with a reason. My hypothesis is that warm water dissolves sugar faster.

cards.back: Something that can change in a test.
cards.say: variable. Something that can change in a test. Temperature can be a variable.

cards.back: A test where only one variable is changed and the others are kept the same.
cards.say: fair test. A test where only one variable is changed and the others are kept the same. To make a fair test, we change only the ramp height.

cards.back: Results that are similar each time you repeat the test.
cards.say: reliable. Results that are similar each time you repeat the test. Repeating a test makes the results more reliable.

cards.back: Very close to the true value.
cards.say: accurate. Very close to the true value. A good ruler gives an accurate length.

cards.back: Facts from tests that show whether an idea is right.
cards.say: evidence. Facts from tests that show whether an idea is right. Our results are evidence for our idea.

cards.back: A chart that uses bars to compare amounts.
cards.say: bar chart. A chart that uses bars to compare amounts. A bar chart shows how many children like each fruit.

cards.back: A device that records measurements automatically.
cards.say: data logger. A device that records measurements automatically. A data logger records the temperature all night.

cards.back: To do the test again to check the results.
cards.say: repeat. To do the test again to check the results. We repeat each test three times.

cards.back: A typical value, found by adding the results and dividing by how many there are.
cards.say: average. A typical value, found by adding the results and dividing by how many there are. The average of two, four and six is four.

cards.back: To suggest a change that would make a test better.
cards.say: improve. To suggest a change that would make a test better. We could improve the test by using a longer ramp.

cards.back: To say how two things are the same and different.
cards.say: compare. To say how two things are the same and different. Compare a frog and a lizard.
